name: Football
description: Football is a high-action Poker variant based on Seven Card Stud, themed around American Football. It is characterized by its numerous wild cards and the 'extra boost' mechanics that mirror scoring in football. In this game, 3s and 6s are wild, and 2s give an extra card when dealt face-up. It is an extremely volatile game where hand rankings frequently reach Five-of-a-Kind, making it a staple of casual Dealer's Choice poker nights.

history.origins: Derived from the older Poker variant 'Baseball,' Football adapted the 'sportndthemed wild card' concept to focus on different numeric values. It emerged in midnd20th century American home games as a more complex and highndscoring alternative to standard Stud.
timeline: 1950s: Becomes a popular variant alongside 'Baseball' in American social clubs.
1980s: Variations involving 'overtime' cards and 'extra points' are documented in poker strategy books.
Present: Remains a favorite 'chaos' game in recreational poker loops.
history.cultural: Often played during major sports events (like the Super Bowl) as a thematic drinking or social game.
history.evolution: The game evolved from Baseball with different wild ranks: 3s and 6s are wild and 2s grant an extra card, creating massive pots and unpredictable showdowns.

setup.players: 2 to 6 players. Limited to 6 due to the 'extra card' rule potentially exhausting the deck.
setup.dealing: Standard Seven Card Stud format: 2 cards face-down, 4 cards face-up, 1 final card face-down.

rules.objective: Form the highest five-card poker hand using your seven (or more) cards and the designated wild cards.
rules.gameplay:
1. Initial Deal: 3 cards (2 down, 1 up). Betting starts with the low card (Bring-In).
2. Streets 4-6: One card dealt face-up per player. Betting occurs after each deal.
3. The 2-Rule: If anyone receives a 2 face-up, they immediately get one extra face-up card before the next player is dealt. Some players may hold more than seven cards.
4. Showdown: Best five-card poker hand wins. 3s and 6s are wild; Five-of-a-Kind is highest.
keyRules: Wild cards: All 3s and 6s are wild and can substitute for any card; Five-of-a-Kind is the highest hand.
Extra card: If a player is dealt a 2 face-up, they immediately receive one extra face-up card before the next player is dealt.
Winning condition: Form the highest five-card poker hand using your seven (or more) cards and the designated wild cards.

strategy.basic: In Football, a 'Natural' hand is almost never enough to win. You must aim for at least Four-of-a-Kind. If you don't start with a wild card (3 or 6) or a high pair, fold early.
strategy.intermediate: Inventory Management: Because 2s give extra cards, having a 2 face-up is a huge advantage. It gives you a wider selection of cards to form your final 5ndcard hand, effectively increasing your 'draw' potential.
strategy.advanced: The 'Scoreboard' Bluff: If your up-cards include two 6s or two 3s (which are wild), opponents will assume you have at least a Full House or better. Use this visible strength to push players off hands that might actually be stronger in the hole.
tips: Keep an eye on the deck. If several players have received extra cards from 2s, the dealer may run out of cards for the final street. In this case, the final card is often dealt as a common 'community card'.
Wild cards are common; don't be afraid to fold a Straight if the board is showing lots of 3s and 6s.

scoring.description: Scored through betting rounds and Poker hand rankings. All 3s and 6s are wild; 2s grant an extra card when dealt face-up. Cash or chip-based play.
scoring.winCondition: Highest 5-card Poker hand at showdown wins the pot. Five-of-a-Kind is highest hand, possible due to wild cards.
